author: John of Damascus
occasion: A brief exegetical note on Christ's baptism with fire, touching on the Spirit's descent, Pentecost, and the final punishing fire, without explicitly citing a biblical verse.
argument: The Spirit descends upon the apostles; the Spirit is God, and God is a consuming fire. Christ is said to baptize with fire because he poured out the grace of Christ on the holy disciples in the form of fiery tongues, or because of the punishing fire to come. That final baptism is not saving but destructive of evil—no longer will evil and sin hold sway—yet it punishes endlessly.
